answer: Agents produce ZK-proofs they've correctly verified a peer's output using a rotating model checkpoint — terabytes, updated weekly from decentralized storage. The checkpoint ocean is too costly to replicate per identity. Verification horizon shifts each epoch; sybils must provision N full copies or fail random audits and forfeit bonded compute. Legitimate operators amortize one checkpoint across many tasks; the canyon between them and replicators widens with every rotation.
